claims.text: AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock may have thin oxide surface films.
AlCrFeNiSi is typically processed using high-thermal-input additive-manufacturing methods.
Binder jetting or 3D ink-extrusion can shape a binder-containing metal-powder green body at ambient temperature.
The green body can subsequently be densified by isothermal sintering.
Controlled co-reduction under an inert or reducing atmosphere is suitable for processing AlCrFeNiSi green bodies.
An initial co-reduction temperature near 765 K is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi.
An isothermal sintering temperature near 1573 K will densify AlCrFeNiSi components.
The proposed route is applicable to miniature AlCrFeNiSi components with features on the order of 100 micrometers.
Isothermal sintering will produce complete inter-diffusion between feedstock constituents.
The proposed route will produce uniform inter-particle bonding.
Full inter-diffusion and isothermal sintering can yield a segregation-free, structurally homogeneous alloy with low residual stress.
Replacing localized laser or electron-beam heating with binder-based shaping and furnace sintering will reduce fabrication thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients will minimize residual-stress accumulation in AlCrFeNiSi components.
The proposed processing route will lower the likelihood of oxide-induced local defects.
Lower residual stress and fewer oxide-induced defects will enhance ductility and mechanical strength.
Binder-processed AlCrFeNiSi parts will have lower residual stresses than conventionally laser- or electron-beam-processed parts.
Binder-processed AlCrFeNiSi parts will have greater strength and ductility than conventionally processed parts.
The proposed route will simplify the post-processing workflow relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
Laser- and electron-beam additive manufacturing produces high thermal gradients that cause significant residual stresses and degraded mechanical behavior.
The optimal AlCrFeNiSi sintering temperature, co-reduction kinetics, scalability, and industrial reproducibility remain uncertain.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis depends on replacing localized high-thermal-load processing with a lower-gradient route, but the experiment requires the two groups to have comparable thermal histories. Making their thermal histories comparable could remove or confound the defining intervention.
